title: LMCache run_script admin endpoint executes caller-supplied Python without authentication
summary: Before 0.5.6, the admin /run_script endpoint was enabled on all interfaces without authentication. Final 0.5.6 disables it by default, but explicitly enabling it still exposes unauthenticated Python execution.

severity.rationale: An enabled, reachable admin endpoint executes arbitrary Python without authentication. The earlier default made this reachable without a special opt-in, warranting action within 24 hours.

affected.note: Before 0.5.6, the endpoint was served by default. In 0.5.6 it is disabled by default and admin HTTP binds to loopback; explicit re-enablement still provides unauthenticated execution. No complete affected introduction range is established here.

exposure: Any untrusted caller reaching an enabled /run_script endpoint can run Python in the LMCache process. Package version alone cannot prove safety when explicit settings override the hardened defaults.

params.instructions: Check LMCache admin API reachability and run_script_api_enabled or --run-script-api-enabled. Upgrade releases before 0.5.6 and verify the endpoint stays disabled; a version check alone is insufficient.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.5.6 or later for hardened defaults and keep /run_script disabled. Verify the admin bind and network controls. Do not expose an explicitly enabled endpoint to untrusted callers.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm /run_script returns 404 with the feature disabled and untrusted networks cannot reach the admin service.
Check explicit configuration overrides after upgrade.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
